symbols.def: Lebesgue density of the \(X\)-marginal of \(P_S\).

symbols.name: f_T
symbols.def: Lebesgue density of \(P_T\).

symbols.name: g_S
symbols.def: Nonsingular source factor \(g_S(x)=x^{-a}f_S(x)\) for \(x>0\), extended continuously to \(x=0\).

symbols.name: g_T
symbols.def: Nonsingular target factor \(g_T(x)=f_T(x)\).

symbols.name: e
symbols.def: Known trial randomization probability \(e(x)=P_S(A=1\mid X=x)\).

symbols.name: \mu_0
symbols.def: Source control response \(\mu_0(x)=\mathbb E_{P_S}[Y\mid A=0,X=x]\).

symbols.name: \mu_1
symbols.def: Source treated response \(\mu_1(x)=\mathbb E_{P_S}[Y\mid A=1,X=x]\).

symbols.name: \mu
symbols.def: Transportable conditional effect \(\mu(x)=\mu_1(x)-\mu_0(x)\).

symbols.name: \tau
symbols.def: Identified observed-law integral \(\tau=\int_0^1\{\mu_1(x)-\mu_0(x)\}f_T(x)\,dx=\mathbb E_{P_T}[\mu(X)]\); under the identification assumptions it equals the target average treatment effect.

symbols.name: r
symbols.def: Transport Riesz weight \(r(x)=f_T(x)/f_S(x)=x^{-a}g_T(x)/g_S(x)\).

symbols.name: Z
symbols.def: Randomized-trial contrast \(Z=AY/e(X)-(1-A)Y/\{1-e(X)\}\).

symbols.name: p
symbols.def: Local-polynomial order \(p=\lceil s\rceil-1\).

symbols.name: C_{\mathrm{LP}}
symbols.def: Operator-norm constant for the order \(p\) boundary local-polynomial remainder on the unit Hölder ball.

symbols.name: \mathcal P_p

symbols.name: K
symbols.def: A fixed nonzero \(C^\infty\) bump supported on \([0,1]\) with Hölder norm at most one.

symbols.name: \rho_n(a,s)

symbols.name: q
symbols.def: Spline degree \(q=\lceil\max\{s,t\}\rceil\).

symbols.name: \mathcal B_{h,J}

symbols.name: c_{\mathrm{OT}}

symbols.name: \widehat P^S_h

symbols.name: \widehat P^T_h

symbols.name: \widehat\Pi_{h,J}
symbols.def: On a positive-interior-mass branch, the unique exact-feasibility or penalized semi-unbalanced entropic optimizer constructed in \(\mathrm{def:ricot\text{-}weights}\); on the zero-interior-mass branch, the zero finite measure is a deterministic fallback and is not asserted to couple a nonzero target marginal.

symbols.name: \widehat\theta_{h,J}
symbols.def: On a positive-interior-mass exact-feasibility branch, the selected nonconstant spline KKT multiplier; on a positive-interior-mass penalized branch, the quadratic-penalty gradient multiplier; on the zero-interior-mass branch, the deterministic zero vector.

symbols.name: \widehat\psi_{h,J}
symbols.space: real vectors indexed by interior target training observations
symbols.def: On a positive-interior-mass optimization branch, the selected target-marginal KKT multiplier, jointly minimum-norm with the calibration multiplier where applicable; on the zero-interior-mass branch, the deterministic zero vector.

symbols.name: \zeta_i^S
symbols.def: Independent standard-normal source multiplier, conditionally generated after observing \(\mathcal D_{n,m}\).

symbols.name: \zeta_j^T
symbols.def: Independent standard-normal target multiplier, conditionally generated after observing \(\mathcal D_{n,m}\).

symbols.name: \mathbb P^*
symbols.def: Conditional law, given \(\mathcal D_{n,m}\), under which all \(\{\zeta_i^S:i=1,\ldots,n\}\) and \(\{\zeta_j^T:j=1,\ldots,m\}\) are mutually independent \(N(0,1)\) variables.

symbols.name: \operatorname{cv}_{1-\gamma/2}
symbols.def: Folded-normal critical value \(\operatorname{cv}_{1-\gamma/2}(u)=\inf\{c:\inf_{|b|\le u}P(|N(b,1)|\le c)\ge1-\gamma/2\}\).

symbols.def: A prespecified finite grid of candidate pairs \((a,s)\), including values on both sides of \(a=1\).

symbols.name: c_{\mathrm{ss}}
symbols.def: Lower persistence constant in the boundary self-similarity condition.

symbols.name: C_{\mathrm{ss}}
symbols.def: Upper persistence constant in the boundary self-similarity condition.

symbols.name: h_0
symbols.def: Largest dyadic scale on which boundary self-similarity is imposed.

symbols.name: \mathcal M^{\mathrm{ss}}_{n,m}(a,s,t)
symbols.def: Boundary self-similar subclass constructed in \(\mathrm{def:self\text{-}similar\text{-}class}\).

symbols.name: J_{\mu,n}
symbols.def: Deterministic interior regression dimension \(J_{\mu,n}=\lceil n^{1/(2s+1)}\rceil\).

symbols.name: J_{r,n}
symbols.def: Deterministic interior calibration dimension \(J_{r,n}=\lceil(n/\log n)^{1/(2t+1)}\rceil\) for \(n\ge2\), with \(J_{r,1}=1\).

symbols.name: \widehat\beta_{k,h,J_{\mu,n}}
symbols.def: Unique fold-trained ridge spline coefficient in \(\mathrm{def:regression\text{-}fit}\).

symbols.name: \widehat\mu_{h,J_{\mu,n}}
symbols.def: Untruncated order- \(p\) boundary local-polynomial fit spliced to an interior regression spline of dimension \(J_{\mu,n}\).

symbols.name: \widehat U^T_{j,h,J_{\mu,n},J_{r,n}}
symbols.def: Fold-held-out target plug-in summand in \(\mathrm{def:foldwise\text{-}inference\text{-}statistics}\).

symbols.name: \widehat U^B_{i,h,J_{\mu,n},J_{r,n}}
symbols.def: Fold-aggregated untruncated boundary local-polynomial linear summand in \(\mathrm{def:foldwise\text{-}inference\text{-}statistics}\).

symbols.name: \mathbb G^{\mathrm{bd},*}_{h,J_{\mu,n},J_{r,n}}
symbols.def: Fold-centered multiplier analogue of the untruncated boundary local-polynomial linear term.

symbols.name: \widetilde r^{\mathrm{KKT}}_{h,J}
symbols.def: On a positive-interior-mass optimization branch, the exponential continuation of the selected primal--dual solution that agrees with the first-marginal density at source training atoms; on the zero-interior-mass branch it is the identically zero deterministic fallback.

symbols.name: \widehat r^{\mathrm{RICOT}}_{h,J}
symbols.def: The pointwise projection of \(\widetilde r^{\mathrm{KKT}}_{h,J}\) onto \([0,(c_{T,+}/c_{S,-})h^{-a}]\), with the identically zero deterministic fallback on a zero-interior-mass branch. It is measurable and bounded, but it need not inherit the raw plan's training-atom spline-calibration equations.

symbols.name: \Delta_{h,J}
symbols.def: Cross-fitted interior calibration residual \(\Delta_{h,J}(v)=m^{-1}\sum_{j=1}^m v(X_j^T)\mathbf 1\{X_j^T\ge h\}-n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^n\widehat r^{\mathrm{RICOT},(-k_S(i))}_{h,J}(X_i)v(X_i)\mathbf 1\{X_i\ge h\}\).

symbols.name: \mathbb G^{\mathrm{cal},*}_{h,J}
symbols.def: Fold-centered source--target calibration-residual multiplier process constructed in \(\mathrm{def:calibration\text{-}residual\text{-}envelope}\).

symbols.name: \widehat\tau^{\mathrm{sp}}_{h,J_{\mu,n},J_{r,n}}
symbols.def: Boundary-spliced Riesz-calibrated transport estimator with separate regression and calibration dimensions.

symbols.name: \widehat U^R_{i,h,J_{\mu,n},J_{r,n}}
symbols.def: Fold-held-out weighted interior residual summand in \(\mathrm{def:foldwise\text{-}inference\text{-}statistics}\).

symbols.name: \widehat E_{h,J_{\mu,n},J_{r,n}}
symbols.def: Conditional multiplier quantile envelope for the joint centered calibration and repaired boundary processes.

symbols.name: \widehat{\mathrm{se}}_{h,J_{\mu,n},J_{r,n}}
symbols.def: Cross-fitted standard-error estimate for the target, interior calibrated residual, and untruncated boundary local-polynomial terms.

symbols.name: C_{n,m}(h)
symbols.def: Fold-varying cross-fitted interior calibration discrepancy defined in \(\mathrm{def:bias\text{-}envelope}\).

symbols.name: \widehat B_{h,J_{\mu,n},J_{r,n}}
symbols.def: Fixed-class upper envelope for boundary smoothing, the observable fold-varying discrepancy, and calibration bias of the repaired spliced estimator.

symbols.name: \mathcal I_{h,J_{\mu,n},J_{r,n}}
symbols.def: Bias-aware interval constructed from the separately tuned regression and calibration statistics.

assumptions.condition: \(e\) is fixed and known by the source-trial randomization protocol.
\(\mathbb E_{F^T_{n,m}}[Y^T(d)\mid X^T=x]=\mathbb E_{F^S_{n,m}}[Y^S(d)\mid X=x]=\mu_d(x)\) for every \(d\in\{0,1\}\) and \(P_T\)-almost every \(x\).

novel.justification: The condition permits polynomial depletion of trial enrollment at a clinically meaningful covariate boundary. Beta-type enrollment densities and smooth exponential tilts of \(x^a\) satisfy it, so it describes a concrete weak-overlap mechanism rather than an estimator-dependent rate restriction.

standard.name: target density bounded away from zero and infinity

assumptions.condition: \(\operatorname{Var}(Y\mid A=d,X=x)\ge M^{-1}\) for every \(d\in\{0,1\}\) and \(P_S\)-almost every \(x\).
\(c_{\mathrm{ss}}h^s\le\inf_{q\in\mathcal P_p}\sup_{x\in[h/2,h]}|\mu(x)-q(x)|\le C_{\mathrm{ss}}h^s\) for every dyadic \(h\le h_0\).

novel.justification: The condition says that a leading boundary feature persists across resolution scales instead of disappearing through accidental polynomial cancellation. Functions of the form \(q(x)+cx^s+r(x)\), with \(c\ne0\), \(q\in\mathcal P_p\), and a smoother remainder \(r\), satisfy it, making the restriction interpretable and testable through adjacent-scale differences.

definitions.name: Polynomial-boundary transport class
definitions.construction: \[\mathcal M_{n,m}(a,s,t)=\bigl\{\mathbb P_{n,m}=P_S^{\otimes n}\otimes P_T^{\otimes m}:\exists(F^S_{n,m},F^T_{n,m})\text{ with }P_S=(\pi_S)_\#F^S_{n,m},\ P_T=(\pi_T)_\#F^T_{n,m},\text{ and every listed member-property assumption holds at the fixed indices }(n,m,a,s,t)\bigr\}.\] The finite-\((n,m)\) class contains no condition on how \(m/n\) behaves along a sequence.

definitions.name: Two-sample minimax root risk
definitions.construction: \[\mathfrak R_{n,m}(a,s,t)=\inf_{\widehat\tau}\sup_{\mathbb P_{n,m}\in\mathcal M_{n,m}(a,s,t)}\Bigl\{\mathbb E_{\mathbb P_{n,m}}[(\widehat\tau-\tau)^2]\Bigr\}^{1/2},\] where the infimum ranges over all estimators measurable with respect to \(\mathcal D_{n,m}\).

definitions.name: Executable cross-fitted boundary regression
definitions.construction:
For each \(k\in\{1,\ldots,K_0\}\), use the source indices in \(\mathcal T^S_k\) and set
\[
\widehat G_{k,h}=\frac1{|\mathcal T^S_k|}\sum_{i\in\mathcal T^S_k}\mathbf 1\{X_i\le2h\}\mathbf R_h(X_i)\mathbf R_h(X_i)^\top+n^{-2}I_{p+1},
\qquad
\widehat\alpha_{k,h}=\widehat G_{k,h}^{-1}\frac1{|\mathcal T^S_k|}\sum_{i\in\mathcal T^S_k}\mathbf 1\{X_i\le2h\}\mathbf R_h(X_i)Z_i.
\]
Using the same training indices with \(X_i\ge h\), let \(\widehat\beta_{k,h,J_{\mu,n}}\) be the unique minimizer over \(\mathbb R^{J_{\mu,n}}\) of
\[
\frac1{|\mathcal T^S_k|}\sum_{i\in\mathcal T^S_k}\mathbf 1\{X_i\ge h\}\{Z_i-\mathbf b_{h,J_{\mu,n}}(X_i)^\top\beta\}^2+n^{-2}\|\beta\|_2^2.
\]
Define the untruncated fit
\[
\widehat\mu^{(-k)}_{h,J_{\mu,n}}(x)=
\begin{cases}
\mathbf R_h(x)^\top\widehat\alpha_{k,h},&0\le x<h,\\
\mathbf b_{h,J_{\mu,n}}(x)^\top\widehat\beta_{k,h,J_{\mu,n}},&h\le x\le1.
\end{cases}
\]
Empty local or interior samples return the unique ridge solution. The positive ridges and ordered bases make every fold fit unique. No clipping map or kink derivative is part of the construction.

definitions.name: Executable interior RiCOT weights
definitions.construction:
For each fold \(k\), form \(\widehat P^{S,(-k)}_h\) and \(\widehat P^{T,(-k)}_h\) from the training complements. If either interior training measure has zero total mass, define \(\widehat\Pi^{(-k)}_{h,J_{r,n}}=0\), set every calibration and target-marginal multiplier to zero, and set both the raw continuation and the capped downstream weight to zero on \([h,1]\). This branch precedes all optimization below.

Suppose now that both interior training measures have positive total mass. Let \(\mathcal F^\circ_{h,J_{r,n},k}\) be the finite plans \(\Pi\) that have strictly positive density relative to \(\widehat P^{S,(-k)}_h\otimes\widehat P^{T,(-k)}_h\), satisfy \(\Pi_2=\widehat P^{T,(-k)}_h\), and satisfy
\[
\int\widetilde{\mathbf b}_{h,J_{r,n}}(x)\,d\Pi_1(x)=\int\widetilde{\mathbf b}_{h,J_{r,n}}(z)\,d\widehat P^{T,(-k)}_h(z).
\]
If \(\mathcal F^\circ_{h,J_{r,n},k}\ne\varnothing\), define \(\widehat\Pi^{(-k)}_{h,J_{r,n}}\) as the unique minimizer over its closure of
\[
\int c_{\mathrm{OT}}(x,z)\,d\Pi+\eta_0\operatorname{KL}(\Pi\,\|\,\widehat P^{S,(-k)}_h\otimes\widehat P^{T,(-k)}_h)+\lambda_0\operatorname{KL}(\Pi_1\,\|\,\widehat P^{S,(-k)}_h).
\]
Otherwise minimize the same strictly convex criterion subject to \(\Pi_2=\widehat P^{T,(-k)}_h\), plus
\[
\xi_n\left\|\int\widetilde{\mathbf b}_{h,J_{r,n}}\,d\Pi_1-\int\widetilde{\mathbf b}_{h,J_{r,n}}(z)\,d\widehat P^{T,(-k)}_h(z)\right\|_2^2.
\]
Generalized Kullback--Leibler divergence is used for finite measures. In the exact-feasibility branch, let \(\widehat\theta^{(-k)}_{h,J_{r,n}}\) and \(\widehat\psi^{(-k)}_{h,J_{r,n},j}\) be the KKT multipliers for the nonconstant calibration and target-marginal equations; among all joint dual solutions choose the pair of smallest Euclidean norm, with lexicographic tie-breaking. In the penalized branch, set
\[
\widehat\delta^{(-k)}_{h,J_{r,n}}=
\int\widetilde{\mathbf b}_{h,J_{r,n}}(x)\,d\widehat\Pi^{(-k)}_{h,J_{r,n},1}(x)
-\int\widetilde{\mathbf b}_{h,J_{r,n}}(z)\,d\widehat P^{T,(-k)}_h(z),
\qquad
\widehat\theta^{(-k)}_{h,J_{r,n}}=2\xi_n\widehat\delta^{(-k)}_{h,J_{r,n}},
\]
which is the gradient multiplier contributed by the quadratic calibration penalty, and let \(\widehat\psi^{(-k)}_{h,J_{r,n},j}\) be a KKT multiplier for the target-marginal equations; among compatible target-marginal multipliers choose the one of smallest Euclidean norm, with lexicographic tie-breaking. For every \(x\in[h,1]\), define the raw KKT continuation
\[
\widetilde r^{\mathrm{KKT},(-k)}_{h,J_{r,n}}(x)=
\left[\frac1{|\mathcal T^T_k|}\sum_{j\in\mathcal T^T_k}\mathbf 1\{X_j^T\ge h\}\exp\left\{-\frac{c_{\mathrm{OT}}(x,X_j^T)+\widehat\theta_{h,J_{r,n}}^{(-k)\top}\widetilde{\mathbf b}_{h,J_{r,n}}(x)+\widehat\psi^{(-k)}_{h,J_{r,n},j}}{\eta_0}\right\}\right]^{\eta_0/(\eta_0+\lambda_0)}
\]
and the capped downstream weight
\[
\widehat r^{\mathrm{RICOT},(-k)}_{h,J_{r,n}}(x)=\min\left\{\widetilde r^{\mathrm{KKT},(-k)}_{h,J_{r,n}}(x),\frac{c_{T,+}}{c_{S,-}}h^{-a}\right\}.
\]
Only \(\widetilde r^{\mathrm{KKT},(-k)}_{h,J_{r,n}}\) is the KKT continuation of \(d\widehat\Pi^{(-k)}_{h,J_{r,n},1}/d\widehat P^{S,(-k)}_h\), and only it agrees with that density at source training atoms. The downstream weight \(\widehat r^{\mathrm{RICOT},(-k)}_{h,J_{r,n}}\) is its pointwise projection onto \([0,(c_{T,+}/c_{S,-})h^{-a}]\). It is positive, measurable, and bounded at held-out points, but after projection it need not satisfy the raw plan's exact spline-calibration equations. The cap does not truncate the oracle ratio on \([h,1]\), because \(r(x)=x^{-a}g_T(x)/g_S(x)\le(c_{T,+}/c_{S,-})h^{-a}\). The deterministic schedules are \(\eta_n=\eta_0\), \(\lambda_n=\lambda_0\), \(\xi_n=n^2\), and \(J=J_{r,n}\); the boundary-splice bandwidth remains \(h=h_n\) and is not used as the calibration dimension.

definitions.name: Riesz-calibrated boundary-spliced estimator
definitions.construction:
Using the fold maps \(k_S\) and \(k_T\) and the unique training-complement fits from \(\mathrm{def:regression\text{-}fit}\) and \(\mathrm{def:ricot\text{-}weights}\), define
\[
\widehat\tau^{\mathrm{sp}}_{h,J_{\mu,n},J_{r,n}}=
\frac1m\sum_{j=1}^m\widehat\mu_{h,J_{\mu,n}}^{(-k_T(j))}(X_j^T)
+\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n\widehat r^{\mathrm{RICOT},(-k_S(i))}_{h,J_{r,n}}(X_i)\mathbf 1\{X_i\ge h\}\{Z_i-\widehat\mu_{h,J_{\mu,n}}^{(-k_S(i))}(X_i)\}.
\]
Every displayed evaluation uses a fit trained without that observation's deterministic fold. The dual extension is evaluated as a function at held-out \(X_i\), not as an empirical-support lookup. If an interior training measure is empty, its weight contribution is zero by \(\mathrm{def:ricot\text{-}weights}\). The regression and calibration dimensions are respectively \(J_{\mu,n}\) and \(J_{r,n}\); only \(h\) is the boundary-splice bandwidth.

definitions.name: Fixed-class bias envelope
definitions.construction:
For every \(h\in(0,1)\), define the observable fold-varying discrepancy
\[
C_{n,m}(h)=\frac1m\sum_{j=1}^m\widehat\mu_{h,J_{\mu,n}}^{(-k_T(j))}(X_j^T)\mathbf 1\{X_j^T\ge h\}-\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n\widehat r^{\mathrm{RICOT},(-k_S(i))}_{h,J_{r,n}}(X_i)\widehat\mu_{h,J_{\mu,n}}^{(-k_S(i))}(X_i)\mathbf 1\{X_i\ge h\}.
\]
Define
\[
\widehat B_{h,J_{\mu,n},J_{r,n}}=2C_{\mathrm{LP}}Mh^{s+1}+|C_{n,m}(h)|+2M\sup_{v\in\mathcal H^s(1)}|\Delta_{h,J_{r,n}}(v)|.
\]
The middle term is required by the exact held-out interior decomposition; it is not generally equal to a calibration residual of one common fitted function. The factor \(2M\) is the Hölder radius inherited by \(\mu=\mu_1-\mu_0\).

definitions.name: Foldwise linear summands and standard error
definitions.construction:
For \(j\in\mathcal V^T_k\) and \(i\in\mathcal V^S_k\), define
\[
\widehat U^T_{j,h,J_{\mu,n},J_{r,n}}=\widehat\mu_{h,J_{\mu,n}}^{(-k)}(X_j^T),
\qquad
\widehat U^R_{i,h,J_{\mu,n},J_{r,n}}=\widehat r^{\mathrm{RICOT},(-k)}_{h,J_{r,n}}(X_i)\mathbf 1\{X_i\ge h\}\{Z_i-\widehat\mu_{h,J_{\mu,n}}^{(-k)}(X_i)\}.
\]
Because the boundary fit is untruncated, its ordinary ridge/local-polynomial linear summand is
\[
\widehat U^B_{i,h,J_{\mu,n},J_{r,n}}=\frac{n}{m}\sum_{k:i\in\mathcal T^S_k}\frac{\mathbf 1\{X_i\le2h\}}{|\mathcal T^S_k|}\left[\sum_{j\in\mathcal V^T_k}\mathbf 1\{X_j^T<h\}\mathbf R_h(X_j^T)^\top\widehat G_{k,h}^{-1}\mathbf R_h(X_i)\right]\{Z_i-\mathbf R_h(X_i)^\top\widehat\alpha_{k,h}\}.
\]
For fold-indexed numbers \((W_u)\), write \(\overline W_k^S=(N_k^S)^{-1}\sum_{i\in\mathcal V^S_k}W_i\) and \(\overline W_k^T=(N_k^T)^{-1}\sum_{j\in\mathcal V^T_k}W_j\). Define
\[
\begin{aligned}
\widehat{\mathrm{se}}_{h,J_{\mu,n},J_{r,n}}^2={}&\frac1{m^2}\sum_{k=1}^{K_0}\frac{N_k^T}{N_k^T-1}\sum_{j\in\mathcal V^T_k}(\widehat U^T_{j,h,J_{\mu,n},J_{r,n}}-\overline{\widehat U^T}_{k,h,J_{\mu,n},J_{r,n}})^2\\
&+\frac1{n^2}\sum_{k=1}^{K_0}\frac{N_k^S}{N_k^S-1}\sum_{i\in\mathcal V^S_k}(\widehat U^R_{i,h,J_{\mu,n},J_{r,n}}-\overline{\widehat U^R}_{k,h,J_{\mu,n},J_{r,n}})^2\\
&+\frac1{n^2}\sum_{k=1}^{K_0}\frac{N_k^S}{N_k^S-1}\sum_{i\in\mathcal V^S_k}(\widehat U^B_{i,h,J_{\mu,n},J_{r,n}}-\overline{\widehat U^B}_{k,h,J_{\mu,n},J_{r,n}})^2\\
&+\frac2{n^2}\sum_{k=1}^{K_0}\frac{N_k^S}{N_k^S-1}\sum_{i\in\mathcal V^S_k}(\widehat U^R_{i,h,J_{\mu,n},J_{r,n}}-\overline{\widehat U^R}_{k,h,J_{\mu,n},J_{r,n}})(\widehat U^B_{i,h,J_{\mu,n},J_{r,n}}-\overline{\widehat U^B}_{k,h,J_{\mu,n},J_{r,n}}).
\end{aligned}
\]
The four lines are the target variance, interior source variance, boundary source variance, and within-source covariance. There is no primitive source--target covariance because \(\mathbb P_{n,m}=P_S^{\otimes n}\otimes P_T^{\otimes m}\). A term with fold size at most one is zero.

definitions.name: Multiplier calibration-residual envelope
definitions.construction:
Conditionally on \(\mathcal D_{n,m}\), let \(\mathbb P^*\) make the source and target multipliers mutually independent standard-normal variables. For \(v\in\mathcal H^s(1)\), define
\[
\begin{aligned}
\mathbb G^{\mathrm{cal},*}_{h,J_{r,n}}(v)={}&\frac1m\sum_{k=1}^{K_0}\sum_{j\in\mathcal V^T_k}\zeta_j^T\left[v(X_j^T)\mathbf 1\{X_j^T\ge h\}-\frac1{N_k^T}\sum_{\ell\in\mathcal V^T_k}v(X_\ell^T)\mathbf 1\{X_\ell^T\ge h\}\right]\\
&-\frac1n\sum_{k=1}^{K_0}\sum_{i\in\mathcal V^S_k}\zeta_i^S\left[\widehat r^{\mathrm{RICOT},(-k)}_{h,J_{r,n}}(X_i)v(X_i)\mathbf 1\{X_i\ge h\}-\frac1{N_k^S}\sum_{\ell\in\mathcal V^S_k}\widehat r^{\mathrm{RICOT},(-k)}_{h,J_{r,n}}(X_\ell)v(X_\ell)\mathbf 1\{X_\ell\ge h\}\right].
\end{aligned}
\]
Define
\[
\mathbb G^{\mathrm{bd},*}_{h,J_{\mu,n},J_{r,n}}=\frac1n\sum_{k=1}^{K_0}\sum_{i\in\mathcal V^S_k}\zeta_i^S\left[\widehat U^B_{i,h,J_{\mu,n},J_{r,n}}-\frac1{N_k^S}\sum_{\ell\in\mathcal V^S_k}\widehat U^B_{\ell,h,J_{\mu,n},J_{r,n}}\right]
\]
and
\[
\widehat E_{h,J_{\mu,n},J_{r,n}}=\inf\left\{e\ge0:\mathbb P^*\left(\sup_{v\in\mathcal H^s(1)}\left|2M\mathbb G^{\mathrm{cal},*}_{h,J_{r,n}}(v)+\mathbb G^{\mathrm{bd},*}_{h,J_{\mu,n},J_{r,n}}\right|\le e\,\middle|\,\mathcal D_{n,m}\right)\ge1-\gamma/2\right\}.
\]
Empty-fold averages are zero. The same source multipliers appear in both source pieces, retaining their covariance, and all target multipliers are independent of all source multipliers.

definitions.name: Bias-aware transported-mean interval
definitions.construction:
Using only the displayed bias, multiplier-envelope, and standard-error statistics, define, when \(\widehat{\mathrm{se}}_{h,J_{\mu,n},J_{r,n}}>0\),
\[
\mathcal I_{h,J_{\mu,n},J_{r,n}}=\left[\widehat\tau^{\mathrm{sp}}_{h,J_{\mu,n},J_{r,n}}\pm\operatorname{cv}_{1-\gamma/2}\!\left(\frac{\widehat B_{h,J_{\mu,n},J_{r,n}}+\widehat E_{h,J_{\mu,n},J_{r,n}}}{\widehat{\mathrm{se}}_{h,J_{\mu,n},J_{r,n}}}\right)\widehat{\mathrm{se}}_{h,J_{\mu,n},J_{r,n}}\right].
\]
If \(\widehat{\mathrm{se}}_{h,J_{\mu,n},J_{r,n}}=0\), define
\[
\mathcal I_{h,J_{\mu,n},J_{r,n}}=\left[\widehat\tau^{\mathrm{sp}}_{h,J_{\mu,n},J_{r,n}}-(\widehat B_{h,J_{\mu,n},J_{r,n}}+\widehat E_{h,J_{\mu,n},J_{r,n}}),\ \widehat\tau^{\mathrm{sp}}_{h,J_{\mu,n},J_{r,n}}+(\widehat B_{h,J_{\mu,n},J_{r,n}}+\widehat E_{h,J_{\mu,n},J_{r,n}})\right].
\]
This is the finite continuous extension of the bias-aware radius and is a singleton if both envelopes vanish.

definitions.name: Multiscale self-similar adaptation handle
definitions.construction: Use dyadic differences of adjacent untruncated boundary local-polynomial fits to estimate persistent boundary approximation error, estimate \(a\) from source empirical masses of dyadic boundary shells, and combine these diagnostics with interior Riesz-calibration residuals to select one interval from \(\{\mathcal I_{h,J_{\mu,n},J_{r,n}}:h\text{ dyadic}\}\). The handle still does not specify the measurable exponent estimators, thresholds, selection rule, or tie breaking.

statements.statement: For every \(\mathbb P_{n,m}\in\mathcal M_{n,m}(a,s,t)\) and \(h\downarrow0\), \[\left\|r\mathbf 1\{X\ge h\}\right\|_{L^2(P_S)}^2=\int_h^1\frac{f_T(x)^2}{f_S(x)}\,dx\asymp\begin{cases}1,&a<1,\\ \log(1/h),&a=1,\\ h^{1-a},&a>1.\end{cases}\] Hence the target expectation functional has a source \(L^2(P_S)\) Riesz representer if and only if \(a<1\).
statements.justification: This norm is the precise regularity threshold behind the regular, critical, and nonregular regimes.
statements.gap: The transported control-regression component in Burman et al.'s distinct target-outcome estimand uses a density-ratio representer under bounded overlap, while Khan and Tamer link large inverse weights to irregularity without computing this polynomial-boundary threshold for the present covariate-only target functional.
statements.consumer: The lemma tells analysts of the RICOT cardiomyopathy transport study whether an ordinary influence-function variance is finite before fitting a transport estimator.
statements.proof_tex:
\textbf{Proof.}
By the definitions of \(r\), \(f_S\), \(f_T\), \(g_S\), and \(g_T\), for every \(h\in(0,1)\),
\[
 \left\|r\mathbf 1\{X\ge h\}\right\|_{L^2(P_S)}^2
 =\int_h^1 r(x)^2 f_S(x)\,dx
 =\int_h^1 \frac{f_T(x)^2}{f_S(x)}\,dx
 =\int_h^1 x^{-a}\frac{g_T(x)^2}{g_S(x)}\,dx.
\]
The source- and target-boundary-factor assumptions give, pointwise on \([0,1]\),
\[
 \frac{c_{T,-}^2}{c_{S,+}}x^{-a}
 \le x^{-a}\frac{g_T(x)^2}{g_S(x)}
 \le \frac{c_{T,+}^2}{c_{S,-}}x^{-a}.
\]
The constants in this comparison are finite and strictly positive.  Direct integration gives
\[
 \int_h^1x^{-a}\,dx=
 \begin{cases}
 (1-h^{1-a})/(1-a),&a<1,\\
 \log(1/h),&a=1,\\
 (h^{1-a}-1)/(a-1),&a>1.
 \end{cases}
\]
This proves the displayed three-regime equivalence, uniformly over members of the class.

It remains to justify the representer assertion.  On \(L^2(P_S)\), the source component of the target-expectation functional is the linear map
\[
 L(v)=\int_0^1v(x)f_T(x)\,dx=\mathbb E_{P_S}\{r(X)v(X)\}.
\]
If \(a<1\), the preceding calculation with \(h\downarrow0\) shows that \(r\in L^2(P_S)\), so Cauchy--Schwarz makes \(L\) continuous and \(r\) is its representer.  Conversely, if \(L\) had an \(L^2(P_S)\) representer \(q\), then for every bounded measurable \(v\),
\[
 \int_0^1v(x)q(x)f_S(x)\,dx=\int_0^1v(x)f_T(x)\,dx.
\]
Because \(f_S(x)>0\) for Lebesgue-almost every \(x\in(0,1]\), uniqueness of Radon--Nikodym derivatives gives \(q=r\), \(P_S\)-almost surely.  For \(a\ge1\), the same integral calculation shows \(r\notin L^2(P_S)\), a contradiction.  Thus a source \(L^2(P_S)\) representer exists if and only if \(a<1\). \(\square\)

statements.statement: Suppose \(t>1/2\), \(s/(2s+1)+t/(2t+1)>1/2\), \(M\ge a+1\), and \(c_{T,-}<1<c_{T,+}\). There are constants \(c,C>0\) such that, for every sufficiently small \(h\), the perturbations generated by \(b_h\) yield two observed-data laws \(\mathbb P_{+,h},\mathbb P_{-,h}\in\mathcal M_{n,m}(a,s,t)\) whose source marginals satisfy \[\operatorname{KL}(P_{+,h}^{S,n},P_{-,h}^{S,n})\le Cnh^{2s+a+1},\qquad |\tau(\mathbb P_{+,h})-\tau(\mathbb P_{-,h})|\ge ch^{s+1}.\] A separate smooth target-density perturbation yields two full-data laws whose observed target projections have divergence bounded by a constant and target separation at least \(cm^{-1/2}\).
statements.justification: The witness converts the boundary geometry into the exact testing separation needed for the converse.
statements.gap: Zhang et al. define \(\mathcal V\) by the uniform bound \(\sup_x p^*(x)/p^\circ(x)\le B\) in Section 1 on page 2 and state its minimax lower bound as Theorem 1 in Appendix A.1 on page 12; that construction does not cover a diverging polynomial boundary ratio, produce the exponent \((s+1)/(2s+a+1)\), or include the independent target-sample floor.
statements.consumer: The witness certifies that no alternative weighting method can improve the proposed cardiomyopathy transport rate merely by changing the optimizer.
statements.proof_tex:
\textbf{Proof.}
We first check that the displayed restriction on \(M\) is exactly the normalization-compatible one for the submodel used below.  If \(f_S(x)=x^ag_S(x)\) is a density and the Hölder norm controls the supremum norm, then
\[
 1=\int_0^1x^ag_S(x)\,dx
 \le \frac{\lVert g_S\rVert_\infty}{a+1}
 \le \frac{M}{a+1}.
\]
Thus nonemptiness requires \(M\ge a+1\) for any radius-\(M\) source factor, and equality permits the constant factor used next.

Put
\[
 f_S(x)=(a+1)x^a,\qquad f_T(x)=1,
\]
so that \(g_S=a+1\) and \(g_T=1\).  The bounds on \(c_{S,-},c_{S,+},c_{T,-},c_{T,+}\), together with \(M\ge a+1\), put these factors in all density-factor conditions, including at equality.  Retain the known propensity \(e\).  Conditional on \(X=x\), take \(Y^S(0)\) and \(Y^S(1)\) to be Bernoulli variables, conditionally independent of \(A\), with
\[
 \mu_{0,\pm}(x)=\frac12,
 \qquad
 \mu_{1,\pm}(x)=\frac12\pm\delta b_h(x).
\]
Give the target potential outcomes the same conditional means.  A smooth compactly supported bump satisfies
\[
 \sup_{0<h\le1}\lVert h^sK(\cdot/h)\mathbf 1_{[0,h]}\rVert_{\mathcal H^s}<\infty.
\]
Choose the fixed \(\delta>0\) small enough that both response functions lie in \(\mathcal H^s(M)\) and \([0,1]\).  Since \(M>4\), it may also be chosen so that
\[
 \operatorname{Var}(Y\mid A=d,X=x)
 \ge \frac14-\delta^2\ge M^{-1}.
\]
Consistency, conditional randomization, mean transportability, treatment positivity, and every remaining member property then hold by construction.  Both full-data laws therefore induce members of \(\mathcal M_{n,m}(a,s,t)\).

For \(|u|\le\delta<1/2\), the elementary inequality
\[
 \operatorname{kl}\!\left(\operatorname{Bern}\left(\frac12+u\right),
 \operatorname{Bern}\left(\frac12-u\right)\right)
 \le C_0u^2
\]
follows from \(\operatorname{kl}(p,q)\le(p-q)^2/\{q(1-q)\}\).  The two source laws differ only in the treated response.  Tensorization and \(e(x)\le1\) give
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \operatorname{KL}(P_{+,h}^{S,n},P_{-,h}^{S,n})
 &\le C_0n\delta^2\int_0^hb_h(x)^2(a+1)x^a\,dx\\
 &=C_0(a+1)\delta^2nh^{2s+a+1}
   \int_0^1K(u)^2u^a\,du
 \le Cnh^{2s+a+1}.
\end{aligned}
\]
Because \(K\ge0\) is nonzero, \(k_1=\int_0^1K(u)\,du>0\).  The observed target covariate law is common to the two experiments, and hence
\[
 |\tau(\mathbb P_{+,h})-\tau(\mathbb P_{-,h})|
 =2\delta\int_0^hb_h(x)\,dx
 =2\delta k_1h^{s+1}\ge ch^{s+1}.
\]

For the independent target-sample witness, use the same density factors but a common nonconstant source contrast.  Let \(\ell(x)=x-1/2\), choose a fixed sufficiently small \(\delta_0>0\), and set
\[
 \mu_0(x)=\frac12,
 \qquad
 \mu_1(x)=\frac12+\delta_0\ell(x).
\]
These smooth armwise regressions satisfy the response and nondegeneracy conditions when \(\delta_0\) is small.  Keep the entire source law fixed and define
\[
 f_{T,\pm}(x)=1\pm u_m\ell(x),
 \qquad
 u_m=\delta_1m^{-1/2}.
\]
Since \(\int_0^1\ell(x)\,dx=0\), both functions integrate to one.  The strict slack \(c_{T,-}<1<c_{T,+}\) permits a fixed \(\delta_1>0\) for which both densities are positive, obey the prescribed bounds, and belong to \(\mathcal H^t(M)\).  With \(f_{T,-}\) bounded away from zero,
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \operatorname{KL}(P_{T,+}^{\otimes m},P_{T,-}^{\otimes m})
 &\le m\int_0^1\frac{\{f_{T,+}(x)-f_{T,-}(x)\}^2}{f_{T,-}(x)}\,dx\\
 &\le C_1mu_m^2\int_0^1\ell(x)^2\,dx
 \le C_2.
\end{aligned}
\]
Assign target potential outcomes the displayed common conditional means.  This supplies full-data extensions satisfying mean transportability, while the observed target projections differ only through \(f_{T,\pm}\).  Finally,
\[
 |\tau_+-\tau_-|
 =2\delta_0u_m\int_0^1\ell(x)^2\,dx
 =\frac{\delta_0\delta_1}{6}m^{-1/2}.
\]
This proves both asserted witnesses. \(\square\)

statements.statement: For fixed \(a,s,t,M,\varepsilon,c_{S,-},c_{S,+},c_{T,-},c_{T,+}\) with \(t>1/2\), \(s/(2s+1)+t/(2t+1)>1/2\), \(M\ge a+1\), and \(c_{T,-}<1<c_{T,+}\), there is \(c>0\) such that \[\mathfrak R_{n,m}(a,s,t)\ge c\{m^{-1/2}+\rho_n(a,s)\}.\] At \(a=1\), the source term is \(c\sqrt{\log n/n}\); it is obtained by a multiscale mixture of boundary bumps and has no hidden polynomial loss.
statements.justification: The converse is the theorem-level certificate that the three regimes are structural rather than artifacts of truncation.
statements.gap: Khan and Tamer establish tail-dependent irregularity. Zhang et al.'s uniformly bounded-ratio class is defined in Section 1 on page 2 and its known-law lower bound is Theorem 1 in Appendix A.1 on page 12; neither result derives the two-sample polynomial-boundary phase diagram or its critical logarithm.
statements.consumer: The result gives trial planners a lower bound on how much source recruitment near an underrepresented cardiomyopathy-risk boundary is needed for a desired precision.
statements.proof_tex:
\textbf{Proof.}
The source-only result \(\mathrm{lem:source\text{-}only\text{-}frontier\text{-}lower}\) gives
\[
\mathfrak R_{n,m}(a,s,t)\ge c_S\rho_n(a,s).
\]
Its construction keeps the target law fixed and therefore does not use strict target-density slack. Under the strict inequalities in the present theorem, the target-density pair in \(\mathrm{lem:boundary\text{-}bump}\) has parameter separation at least \(c_Tm^{-1/2}\). The construction in that established lemma permits its fixed perturbation multiplier to be chosen small enough that the product Kullback--Leibler divergence is a sufficiently small constant. The testing inequality proved in \(\mathrm{lem:source\text{-}only\text{-}frontier\text{-}lower}\) therefore gives
\[
\mathfrak R_{n,m}(a,s,t)\ge c_T'm^{-1/2}.
\]
Taking the maximum of the source and target bounds and using \(\max\{u,v\}\ge(u+v)/2\) proves
\[
\mathfrak R_{n,m}(a,s,t)\ge c\{m^{-1/2}+\rho_n(a,s)\}.
\]
The source helper's multiscale calculation gives the stated \(\sqrt{\log n/n}\) term at \(a=1\). \(\square\)

statements.statement:
For fixed \(a,s,t,M\) with the separate conditions \(t>1/2\), \(s/(2s+1)+t/(2t+1)>1/2\), and \(a<2t(2s+1)\), along every triangular-array sequence with \(m/n\to\kappa\), the deterministic choices \(h=h_n\), \(J_\mu=J_{\mu,n}\), and \(J_r=J_{r,n}\) give
\[
\sup_{\mathbb P_{n,m}\in\mathcal M_{n,m}(a,s,t)}\Bigl\{\mathbb E_{\mathbb P_{n,m}}[(\widehat\tau^{\mathrm{sp}}_{h_n,J_{\mu,n},J_{r,n}}-\tau)^2]\Bigr\}^{1/2}\le C\{m^{-1/2}+\rho_n(a,s)\}.
\]
Uniformly over the same sequence, the fold-trained dual extensions evaluated on their held-out source folds obey
\[
\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n\{\widehat r^{\mathrm{RICOT},(-k_S(i))}_{h_n,J_{r,n}}(X_i)\}^2\mathbf 1\{X_i\ge h_n\}=O_P\!\left(1+\log(1/h_n)\mathbf 1\{a=1\}+h_n^{1-a}\mathbf 1\{a>1\}\right)
\]
and
\[
\frac{\max_{i:X_i\ge h_n}\{\widehat r^{\mathrm{RICOT},(-k_S(i))}_{h_n,J_{r,n}}(X_i)\}^2}{\sum_{i=1}^n\{\widehat r^{\mathrm{RICOT},(-k_S(i))}_{h_n,J_{r,n}}(X_i)\}^2\mathbf 1\{X_i\ge h_n\}}=o_P(1),
\]
with the ratio defined as zero when the denominator is zero. The threshold \(t>1/2\) controls approximation of the one-dimensional density-ratio calibration sieve, whereas the product relation controls the distinct nuisance-product remainder. These out-of-sample stability bounds are conclusions to be derived from the primal program, normalized dual extension, spline geometry, and primitive density conditions, not model assumptions.
statements.justification: The repaired candidate is explicit and separately tuned, but its empirical KKT localization is the unresolved mathematical crux.
statements.gap: Published RiCOT rates assume quantitative optimizer and offset stability and bounded overlap; they do not derive the requested polynomial-boundary localization.
statements.consumer: Closure would turn boundary-overlap diagnostics into a computable precision analysis for the RICOT cardiomyopathy application.

statements.statement:
Under \(t>1/2\) and \(s/(2s+1)+t/(2t+1)>1/2\), in the special case \(a=0\),
\[
\frac{c_{T,-}}{c_{S,+}}\le r(x)=\frac{g_T(x)}{g_S(x)}\le\frac{c_{T,+}}{c_{S,-}},\qquad 0\le x\le1,
\]
\(h_n=n^{-1/\{2(s+1)\}}\), and
\[
h_n^{s+1}=n^{-1/2},\qquad \int_{h_n}^1\frac{f_T(x)^2}{f_S(x)}\,dx=O(1).
\]
For every fold whose source and target interior training measures are both nonzero, the dual extension \(\widehat r^{\mathrm{RICOT},(-k)}_{h_n,J_{r,n}}(x)\) is strictly positive for every \(x\in[h_n,1]\). These deterministic facts do not by themselves assert an empirical norm bound, a nonzero realized residual sum, or a root-risk bound.
statements.justification: The bounded-ratio arithmetic is proved, while the empirical root-risk conclusion correctly remains downstream of attainment.
statements.gap: Positivity of the extension is not a variance or risk bound.
statements.consumer: The case remains a future implementation unit test for nonzero held-out corrections and regular two-sample scaling.

statements.statement:
For fixed \(a,s,t,M\) with \(M\ge a+1\), \(t>1/2\), and \(s/(2s+1)+t/(2t+1)>1/2\), along every sequence with \(m/n\to\kappa\), there is \(c>0\) such that
\[
\mathfrak R_{n,m}(a,s,t)\ge c\left\{m^{-1/2}+\begin{cases}
n^{-1/2},&a<1,\\
\sqrt{\log n/n},&a=1,\\
n^{-(s+1)/(2s+a+1)},&a>1.
\end{cases}\right\}.
\]
This lower phase diagram requires no strict slack in the target-density bounds. Moreover, uniformly over \(\mathbb P_{n,m}\in\mathcal M_{n,m}(a,s,t)\),
\[
m^{-1/2}+h_n^{s+1}+n^{-1/2}\left\|r\mathbf 1\{X\ge h_n\}\right\|_{L^2(P_S)}
\asymp m^{-1/2}+\rho_n(a,s).
\]
Thus the proved minimax lower frontier matches the exact truncated-oracle envelope; no data-driven minimax upper bound is asserted.
statements.justification: The corrected node states the maximal proved lower frontier and its matching truncated-oracle benchmark.
statements.gap: A measurable data-driven minimax upper witness remains unavailable because empirical RiCOT stability is unresolved.
statements.consumer: The result provides a precision impossibility and oracle-benchmark phase diagram for transported effects.

statements.statement:
For fixed \((a,s,t,M)\) with \(s>1/2\), \(t>1/2\), \(s/(2s+1)+t/(2t+1)>1/2\), and \(a<2t(2s+1)\), along every triangular-array sequence satisfying \(m/n\to\kappa\), the interval \(\mathcal I_{h_n,J_{\mu,n},J_{r,n}}\), with the finite zero-standard-error convention in \(\mathrm{def:bias\text{-}aware\text{-}interval}\), obeys
\[
\liminf_{n,m\to\infty}\inf_{\mathbb P_{n,m}\in\mathcal M_{n,m}(a,s,t)}\mathbb P_{n,m}\{\tau\in\mathcal I_{h_n,J_{\mu,n},J_{r,n}}\}\ge1-\gamma,
\]
and its maximal expected length is at most \(C\{m^{-1/2}+\rho_n(a,s)\}\). Uniformly over the class, the explicit four-term statistic \(\widehat{\mathrm{se}}_{h_n,J_{\mu,n},J_{r,n}}^2\), including the covariance between \(\widehat U^R_{i,h_n,J_{\mu,n},J_{r,n}}\) and \(\widehat U^B_{i,h_n,J_{\mu,n},J_{r,n}}\), divided by the variance of the corresponding foldwise linear term converges in probability to one. The studentized linear term has Kolmogorov distance \(o(1)\) from \(N(0,1)\), and conditionally on \(\mathcal D_{n,m}\) the law of
\[
\sup_{v\in\mathcal H^s(1)}|2M\mathbb G^{\mathrm{cal},*}_{h_n,J_{r,n}}(v)+\mathbb G^{\mathrm{bd},*}_{h_n,J_{\mu,n},J_{r,n}}|
\]
approximates its centered sampling analogue with error \(o(1)\). The threshold \(s>1/2\) gives the finite one-dimensional Hölder entropy integral, \(t>1/2\) controls the density-ratio calibration sieve, and the product relation controls the nuisance-product remainder. The conclusion includes \(a=1\), where the normal approximation is scaled by \(\sqrt{\log n/n}\) and the \(2M\) boundary-bias envelope remains explicit.
statements.justification: The corrected interval is evaluable, but its coverage and length guarantees require the unresolved optimizer, Gaussian, multiplier, and moment bounds.
statements.gap: Folded-normal critical values solve the bias-aware decision step only after the stochastic approximation has been proved.
statements.consumer: The interval remains a prespecifiable research candidate for cardiomyopathy transport analyses, not a validated inferential procedure.

statements.statement: Fix \(a>1\), \(t>1/2\), and \(0<s_1<s_2\) such that \(s_\ell/(2s_\ell+1)+t/(2t+1)>1/2\) for \(\ell\in\{1,2\}\), and suppose \(M\ge a+1\) and \(c_{T,-}<1<c_{T,+}\). Any confidence interval with asymptotic coverage at least \(1-\gamma\) uniformly over \(\mathcal M_{n,m}(a,s_1,t)\cup\mathcal M_{n,m}(a,s_2,t)\) has, at some law in \(\mathcal M_{n,m}(a,s_2,t)\), expected length at least \(c\{m^{-1/2}+n^{-(s_1+1)/(2s_1+a+1)}\}\).
statements.justification: The theorem prevents data-driven smoothness selection from being advertised as honest without an explicit restriction that makes boundary bias observable.
statements.gap: Cai and Low characterize adaptation by between-class moduli, but the ordered modulus for a transported functional under source density \(x^a\), including the transition through \(a=1\), has not been computed.
statements.consumer: The result tells clinical transport analysts when prespecifying a smoothness class is unavoidable for valid interval length claims.
statements.proof_tex:
\textbf{Proof.}
We construct both testing alternatives around one common nonconstant smooth baseline.  Let
\[
 f_S(x)=(a+1)x^a,
 \qquad
 f_T(x)=1,
 \qquad
 \ell(x)=x-\frac12.
\]
Choose a fixed sufficiently small \(\delta_0>0\), and take Bernoulli potential outcomes with
\[
 \mu_0(x)=\frac12,
 \qquad
 \mu_1(x)=\frac12+\delta_0\ell(x).
\]
Use the known propensity and make treatment conditionally independent of the potential outcomes.  Because \(\ell\) is smooth, small \(\delta_0\) places both regressions strictly inside the radius-\(M\) balls for orders \(s_1\) and \(s_2\), keeps their values in \([0,1]\), and preserves the variance lower bound.  The condition \(M\ge a+1\) admits the constant source factor \(g_S=a+1\), and the remaining density conditions hold for \(g_T=1\).  Denote the resulting observed law by \(P_0\).  It belongs to \(\mathcal M_{n,m}(a,s_2,t)\), and in fact its regressions belong to both smoothness classes.

Set
\[
 h=n^{-1/(2s_1+a+1)}.
\]
Form \(P_1^S\) by replacing the treated regression by
\[
 \mu_{1,1}(x)=\frac12+\delta_0\ell(x)+\delta b_h(x),
\]
where \(\delta>0\) is a sufficiently small fixed constant; leave every other component unchanged.  Smooth scaling of \(b_h\) puts \(P_1^S\) in \(\mathcal M_{n,m}(a,s_1,t)\).  The same Bernoulli calculation as in \(\mathrm{lem:boundary\text{-}bump}\), now relative to the common nonconstant baseline whose probabilities stay uniformly away from zero and one, gives
\[
 \operatorname{KL}((P_1^S)^{\otimes n},(P_0^S)^{\otimes n})
 \le Cn\delta^2h^{2s_1+a+1}
 =C\delta^2,
\]
and
\[
 |\tau(P_1^S)-\tau(P_0)|
 =\delta h^{s_1+1}\int_0^1K(u)\,du
 \ge c n^{-(s_1+1)/(2s_1+a+1)}.
\]
Choose \(\delta\) so that Pinsker's inequality makes the total-variation distance at most a fixed \(\eta<1-2\gamma\).

Let \(C_{n,m}\) be any interval with the asserted uniform asymptotic coverage.  Under \(P_0\),
\[
 P_0\{\tau(P_0)\in C_{n,m}\}\ge1-\gamma-o(1).
\]
Coverage under \(P_1^S\) and the total-variation inequality imply
\[
 P_0\{\tau(P_1^S)\in C_{n,m}\}
 \ge1-\gamma-\eta-o(1).
\]
The intersection of these two events has \(P_0\)-probability at least \(1-2\gamma-\eta-o(1)\), a positive constant.  On that intersection the interval length is at least the source separation.  Consequently
\[
 \mathbb E_{P_0}|C_{n,m}|
 \ge c_1n^{-(s_1+1)/(2s_1+a+1)}.
\]

For the second alternative, retain exactly the same nonconstant source law and armwise regressions, and replace only the target density by
\[
 f_{T,1}(x)=1+u_m\ell(x),
 \qquad
 u_m=\delta_1m^{-1/2}.
\]
The strict inequalities \(c_{T,-}<1<c_{T,+}\) allow a fixed small \(\delta_1>0\) for which this is an admissible \(\mathcal H^t(M)\) density.  This alternative belongs to both smoothness classes.  Relative to the same baseline \(P_0\),
\[
 \operatorname{KL}(P_{T,1}^{\otimes m},P_{T,0}^{\otimes m})
 \le Cmu_m^2\int_0^1\ell(x)^2\,dx
 \le C\delta_1^2,
\]
whereas the nonconstant contrast gives the explicit separation
\[
 |\tau(P_{T,1})-\tau(P_0)|
 =\delta_0u_m\int_0^1\ell(x)^2\,dx
 =\frac{\delta_0\delta_1}{12}m^{-1/2}.
\]
Choose \(\delta_1\) so that the total-variation distance is also smaller than \(1-2\gamma\).  Repeating the same coverage-intersection argument, still at the identical smoother law \(P_0\), yields
\[
 \mathbb E_{P_0}|C_{n,m}|\ge c_2m^{-1/2}.
\]
Since both inequalities hold at the same \(P_0\in\mathcal M_{n,m}(a,s_2,t)\) and \(\max\{u,v\}\ge(u+v)/2\), the claimed sum lower bound follows. \(\square\)

statements.statement: For the deterministic regime bandwidth \(h_n\), the truncated oracle representer obeys \[m^{-1/2}+h_n^{s+1}+n^{-1/2}\left\|r\mathbf 1\{X\ge h_n\}\right\|_{L^2(P_S)}\asymp m^{-1/2}+\rho_n(a,s).\] Thus the exact boundary-bias and oracle source-standard-deviation balance has the regular, critical, and nonregular rates in \(\mathrm{def:frontier\text{-}rate}\).
statements.proof_tex:
\textbf{Proof.}
By \(\mathrm{lem:riesz\text{-}threshold}\), uniformly over the model class,
\[
 \left\|r\mathbf 1\{X\ge h\}\right\|_{L^2(P_S)}
 \asymp
 \begin{cases}
 1,&a<1,\\
 \sqrt{\log(1/h)},&a=1,\\
 h^{(1-a)/2},&a>1.
 \end{cases}
\]
If \(a<1\), then \(h_n=n^{-1/\{2(s+1)\}}\), so \(h_n^{s+1}=n^{-1/2}\), and the oracle stochastic term is also of order \(n^{-1/2}\).  If \(a=1\), then
\[
 h_n^{s+1}=\sqrt{\frac{\log n}{n}},
 \qquad
 \log(1/h_n)=\frac{\log n-\log\log n}{2(s+1)}\asymp\log n,
\]
and hence \(n^{-1/2}\sqrt{\log(1/h_n)}\asymp\sqrt{\log n/n}\).  If \(a>1\), writing \(D=2s+a+1\) gives
\[
 h_n^{s+1}=n^{-(s+1)/D},
\]
and
\[
 n^{-1/2}h_n^{(1-a)/2}
 =n^{-1/2+(a-1)/(2D)}
 =n^{-(s+1)/D}.
\]
The three cases are exactly \(\rho_n(a,s)\); adding the independent term \(m^{-1/2}\) proves the claim. \(\square\)

statements.statement:
For fixed \(a,s,t,M,\varepsilon,c_{S,-},c_{S,+},c_{T,-},c_{T,+}\) with \(t>1/2\), \(s/(2s+1)+t/(2t+1)>1/2\), and \(M\ge a+1\), there is \(c>0\) such that, for all sufficiently large \(n\) and every \(m\),
\[
\mathfrak R_{n,m}(a,s,t)\ge c\rho_n(a,s).
\]
No strict inequality in the target-density bounds is required. At \(a=1\), the source lower bound is \(c\sqrt{\log n/n}\) and is generated by a multiscale sign mixture whose target covariate law is common to all mixture components.
statements.justification: This source-only converse removes an unnecessary target-density-slack restriction from the lower phase diagram.
statements.gap: A one-bump argument gives the nonregular branch but not the critical logarithm; the proof supplies the required multiscale mixture.
statements.consumer: The lemma is the no-slack lower-bound input for the repaired frontier theorem.
statements.proof_tex:
\textbf{Proof.}
We first record the elementary testing inequality used below. If probability laws \(Q_0,Q_1\) have parameter values separated by \(d>0\), the decision rule that selects the parameter value nearest an arbitrary estimator \(\widehat\tau\) makes an error only on an event where the squared estimation loss is at least \(d^2/4\). Since the sum of the two testing errors is at least \(1-\lVert Q_0-Q_1\rVert_{\mathrm{TV}}\),
\[
\max_{u\in\{0,1\}}\mathbb E_{Q_u}(\widehat\tau-\tau_u)^2
\ge \frac{d^2}{8}\{1-\lVert Q_0-Q_1\rVert_{\mathrm{TV}}\}.
\]
For completeness, the scalar log-sum inequality applied to an event attaining total variation reduces the comparison to Bernoulli laws; the second-derivative bound for binary relative entropy gives
\[
\lVert Q_0-Q_1\rVert_{\mathrm{TV}}^2\le\frac12\operatorname{KL}(Q_0,Q_1).
\]
Thus a pair with sufficiently small constant Kullback--Leibler divergence yields root risk bounded below by a constant multiple of its parameter separation.

Use throughout
\[
f_S(x)=(a+1)x^a,
\qquad
f_T(x)=1.
\]
Then \(g_S=a+1\) and \(g_T=1\). The declared parameter ranges imply
\[
c_{S,-}\le a+1\le c_{S,+},
\qquad
c_{T,-}\le1\le c_{T,+},
\]
and \(M\ge a+1\) gives the source-factor Hölder bound. Hence no strict target-density slack is needed. Let treatment follow the fixed known propensity \(e\). Conditional on \(X\), construct Bernoulli potential outcomes independent of treatment with the conditional means specified below, and give the target potential outcomes the same conditional means. A sufficiently small fixed perturbation constant keeps all means in \([0,1]\), preserves both armwise Hölder bounds, and ensures
\[
\operatorname{Var}(Y\mid A=d,X=x)\ge M^{-1}.
\]
Consistency, conditional randomization, mean transportability, treatment positivity, the density conditions, and all remaining member properties of \(\mathcal M_{n,m}(a,s,t)\) then hold. The target covariate law is the same under every source alternative below, so target observations contribute zero divergence.

Suppose first that \(a>1\). For \(h\in(0,1)\), put
\[
\mu_{0,\pm}(x)=\frac12,
\qquad
\mu_{1,\pm}(x)=\frac12\pm\delta b_h(x).
\]
Smooth scaling of the fixed bump makes these regressions admissible for a sufficiently small \(\delta>0\). The Bernoulli relative-entropy inequality
\[
\operatorname{kl}\!\left(\operatorname{Bern}\left(\frac12+u\right),
\operatorname{Bern}\left(\frac12-u\right)\right)\le C_0u^2,
\qquad |u|\le\delta,
\]
together with \(e(x)\le1\), gives
\[
\operatorname{KL}(P_{+,h}^{S,n},P_{-,h}^{S,n})
\le Cn\int_0^h b_h(x)^2x^a\,dx
\le Cnh^{2s+a+1}.
\]
Because \(K\) is nonnegative and nonzero, \(k_1=\int_0^1K(u)\,du>0\), and
\[
|\tau_+-\tau_-|
=2\delta h^{s+1}k_1.
\]
Taking \(h=c_0n^{-1/(2s+a+1)}\), with a fixed \(c_0>0\) small enough that the product divergence is sufficiently small, the testing inequality yields
\[
\mathfrak R_{n,m}(a,s,t)
\ge c n^{-(s+1)/(2s+a+1)}.
\]

If \(a<1\), choose a nonnegative nonzero \(C^\infty\) function \(q\) supported in \([1/4,3/4]\), and set
\[
\mu_{0,\pm}(x)=\frac12,
\qquad
\mu_{1,\pm}(x)=\frac12\pm\delta n^{-1/2}q(x).
\]
On the support of \(q\), the source density is bounded above, so
\[
\operatorname{KL}(P_+^{S,n},P_-^{S,n})\le C\delta^2.
\]
At the same time,
\[
|\tau_+-\tau_-|
=2\delta n^{-1/2}\int_0^1q(x)\,dx
\ge c n^{-1/2}.
\]
Choosing \(\delta\) small and applying the testing inequality proves the regular source lower bound.

It remains to treat \(a=1\). Let \(\ell_j=2^{-j}\), fix \(j_0\), and choose \(L\) so that
\[
\ell_L\asymp n^{-1/\{2(s+1)\}},
\qquad
L-j_0+1\asymp\log n.
\]
For \(j=j_0,\ldots,L\), define
\[
\phi_j(x)=\frac{\delta}{\sqrt n\,\ell_j}
K\!\left(\frac{x-\ell_j}{\ell_j}\right)
\mathbf 1\{\ell_j\le x\le2\ell_j\},
\]
and, for \(\omega\in\{-1,1\}^{L-j_0+1}\), set
\[
\mu_{0,\omega}(x)=\frac12,
\qquad
\mu_{1,\omega}(x)=\frac12+\sum_{j=j_0}^L\omega_j\phi_j(x).
\]
The choice of \(L\) implies
\[
(\sqrt n\,\ell_j)^{-1}\le C\ell_j^s.
\]
Smooth scaling, disjoint dyadic interiors, and the vanishing of the compactly supported smooth bump at shell endpoints give a common \(\mathcal H^s(M)\) bound. A sufficiently small \(\delta\) therefore makes every sign alternative a member of the model.

The contribution of coordinate \(j\) to the target is
\[
d_j=\int_{\ell_j}^{2\ell_j}\phi_j(x)\,dx
=\frac{\delta k_1}{\sqrt n}.
\]
Since \(f_S(x)=2x\), flipping only \(\omega_j\) changes the source experiment by
\[
\operatorname{KL}(P_\omega^{S,n},P_{\omega^{(j)}}^{S,n})
\le Cn\int_{\ell_j}^{2\ell_j}\phi_j(x)^2x\,dx
\le C\delta^2,
\]
uniformly in \(j\) and the other signs.

Place the uniform product prior on \(\omega\). Conditional on the data, the likelihood and posterior factor over the shells because each observation belongs to at most one shell. Since conditional expectation minimizes squared error,
\[
\inf_{\widehat\tau}\mathbb E_\Pi(\widehat\tau-\tau_\omega)^2
\ge
\mathbb E_\Pi\operatorname{Var}(\tau_\omega\mid\mathcal D_{n,m})
=\sum_{j=j_0}^Ld_j^2\,
\mathbb E_\Pi\operatorname{Var}(\omega_j\mid\mathcal D_{n,m}).
\]
If \(q_j=\mathbb E_\Pi(\omega_j\mid\mathcal D_{n,m})\), then
\[
\operatorname{Var}(\omega_j\mid\mathcal D_{n,m})=1-q_j^2\ge1-|q_j|.
\]
Under the prior predictive law, direct substitution of the two mixture densities shows that \(\mathbb E_\Pi|q_j|\) equals the total-variation distance between the mixture experiments obtained by fixing \(\omega_j=1\) and \(\omega_j=-1\). Joint convexity of relative entropy, which is the log-sum inequality integrated over the sample space, bounds their divergence by the average neighboring divergence and hence by \(C\delta^2\). The preceding total-variation inequality and a sufficiently small fixed \(\delta\) give
\[
\mathbb E_\Pi(1-|q_j|)\ge c_1>0
\]
uniformly in \(j\). Consequently,
\[
\inf_{\widehat\tau}\sup_\omega
\mathbb E_\omega(\widehat\tau-\tau_\omega)^2
\ge c_1\sum_{j=j_0}^Ld_j^2
\ge c\frac{\log n}{n}.
\]
Taking square roots proves the critical lower bound without polynomial loss. The three cases prove the lemma. \(\square\)

statements.statement: For fixed spline degree and equally spaced knots on \([h,1]\), the normalized local B-spline basis has uniformly bounded overlap and a partition of unity; its Lebesgue Gram matrix has eigenvalues comparable to \(J^{-1}\); and every radius-one Hölder function of order \(u\) has a spline approximant with uniform error at most \(C J^{-u}\), where \(C\) depends only on \(u\) and the degree.

statements.statement:
If \(A_1,\ldots,A_N\) are independent centered self-adjoint matrices of dimension \(d\), \(\|A_i\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le L\) almost surely, and \(\|\sum_i\mathbb E(A_i^2)\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le v\), then for every \(x>0\),
\[
\mathbb P\left\{\left\|\sum_{i=1}^NA_i\right\|_{\mathrm{op}}\ge x\right\}
\le2d\exp\left\{-\frac{x^2/2}{v+Lx/3}\right\}.
\]

attestation.note: Stable arXiv handle supplied for the bounded self-adjoint matrix Bernstein inequality.

statements.statement:
There is a universal constant \(C\) such that, for independent centered real variables \(W_1,\ldots,W_N\) with \(0<\sigma^2=\sum_i\mathbb E(W_i^2)<\infty\) and \(\sum_i\mathbb E|W_i|^3<\infty\),
\[
\sup_z\left|\mathbb P\left\{\sigma^{-1}\sum_iW_i\le z\right\}-\Phi(z)\right|
\le C\sigma^{-3}\sum_i\mathbb E|W_i|^3.
\]

statements.statement: The multiscale handle in \(\mathrm{def:adaptive\text{-}handle}\) does not, as presently constructed, define a single interval-valued statistic. It specifies neither measurable exponent estimators, thresholds, a selection rule, nor tie breaking. Consequently the frozen construction has no coverage probability or expected length to evaluate and does not yield the proposed adaptive guarantee. A positive result requires a new executable construction before self-similarity can be used to prove adaptation.
statements.justification: This negative answer isolates the formal obstruction before any adaptive coverage claim is attempted.
statements.gap: The frozen multiscale handle is descriptive rather than an executable selection rule, so existing self-similarity theory cannot yet be applied to it.
statements.consumer: A downstream construction must specify the measurable diagnostics, thresholds, selection map, and tie breaking before it can be used in the RICOT cardiomyopathy analysis.

sampling_model.design: At each triangular-array index \((n,m)\), the observed law is \(\mathbb P_{n,m}=P_S^{\otimes n}\otimes P_T^{\otimes m}\), induced by full-data laws \(F^S_{n,m}\) and \(F^T_{n,m}\) through the projections \(\pi_S\) and \(\pi_T\). The condition \(m/n\to\kappa\) applies only to theorem sequences.
sampling_model.units: Source full-data units are \(W^S=(X,A,Y^S(0),Y^S(1))\) and are observed as \(O^S=\pi_S(W^S)=(X,A,Y)\); target full-data units are \(W^T=(X^T,Y^T(0),Y^T(1))\) and are observed only as \(X^T=\pi_T(W^T)\).
sampling_model.treatment: Binary source treatment has known probability \(e(X)\in[\varepsilon,1-\varepsilon]\).
sampling_model.overlap: The source density is \(f_S(x)=x^ag_S(x)\), where \(c_{S,-}\le g_S\le c_{S,+}\) and \(0<c_{S,-}\le a+1\le c_{S,+}\); the target density is \(f_T(x)=g_T(x)\), where \(c_{T,-}\le g_T\le c_{T,+}\) and \(0<c_{T,-}\le1\le c_{T,+}\).
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Under the separate primitive conditions \(t>1/2\) for the one-dimensional density-ratio calibration sieve and \(s/(2s+1)+t/(2t+1)>1/2\) for the nuisance-product remainder, deterministic five-fold regression uses ridge-regularized order-\(p\) boundary local polynomials and degree-\(q\) interior B-splines. Interior weights solve the squared-distance semi-unbalanced entropic program with schedules \(\eta_n=\eta_0\), \(\lambda_n=\lambda_0\), \(\xi_n=n^2\), equally spaced knots, and \(J_n=\lceil h_n^{-1}\rceil\); normalized dual potentials give a measurable exponential extension evaluated on held-out source covariates. Inference uses the displayed fold-centered source and target multiplier process and the displayed target, interior-source, boundary-source, and source-covariance variance terms.

estimand_functional: \(\tau=\mathbb E_{P_T}[\mu(X)]=\int_0^1\{\mu_1(x)-\mu_0(x)\}f_T(x)\,dx\), targeted by \(\widehat\tau^{\mathrm{sp}}_{h_n,J_{\mu,n},J_{r,n}}\) using the capped downstream RiCOT weight; the raw KKT continuation alone agrees with the training-atom first-marginal density. The proved results are the source-only minimax lower phase diagram and the matching truncated-oracle envelope. Held-out capped-weight localization, RiCOT root-mean-square attainment, Gaussian and multiplier approximation, coverage, and the expected-length guarantee for the bias-aware interval remain open.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: For target data containing treated outcomes, Proposition 2.1 and Theorem 3.1 identify a distinct target-outcome estimand and its efficient influence function. Their calibrated-weight rates use bounded population overlap and Supplementary Assumption S2, including quantitative interiority, bounded plan-to-source ratios, and convergence of the empirical transport offset; strict interiority alone gives positivity but not the uniform bounds needed here.
Inverse-weighted parameters can be irregular and converge slower than the parametric rate when identification uses arbitrarily large weights.
The class \(\mathcal V\) in Section 1, page 2, imposes \(\sup_x p^*(x)/p^\circ(x)\le B\), and Theorem 1 in Appendix A.1, page 12, gives its moment-estimation minimax lower bound.
Folded-normal critical values deliver honest fixed-class local-polynomial confidence intervals with near-optimal expected length.
A bandwidth-indexed Gaussian-process critical value restores coverage after inspecting multiple bandwidths, including overlap-trimming applications.
Trimmed inverse-probability weighting can have Gaussian or non-Gaussian limits, and local-polynomial bias correction plus subsampling yields robust inference.
Between-class and ordered moduli determine lower bounds and constructions for adaptive confidence intervals on linear functionals.
Self-similarity is necessary and sufficient for honest adaptive confidence bands in the Hölder settings studied there.

tldr: A randomized trial may contain progressively fewer patients near a clinically important covariate boundary even when the real-world target population retains positive mass there. In the full-data triangular-array model, the causal target is identified as the observed-law integral \(\tau=\int_0^1\{\mu_1(x)-\mu_0(x)\}f_T(x)\,dx\). The source contribution to root mean-squared error is \(n^{-1/2}\) below the square-integrability threshold \(a=1\), becomes \(\sqrt{\log n/n}\) at the threshold, and is \(n^{-(s+1)/(2s+a+1)}\) above it, in addition to the independent target-sample term \(m^{-1/2}\). Under the separate conditions \(t>1/2\) for the one-dimensional density-ratio calibration sieve and \(s/(2s+1)+t/(2t+1)>1/2\) for the nuisance-product remainder, a fully specified squared-distance Riesz-calibrated semi-unbalanced transport program is truncated to the overlap interior and spliced to a deterministic boundary local polynomial. Matching bump and multiscale lower bounds, a fully evaluable fixed-Hölder-class interval with a \(2M\) bias envelope and explicit foldwise multiplier and covariance terms, and a nonadaptation theorem complete the fixed-class program; honest joint adaptation is posed only on an explicit boundary self-similar subclass.

project_justification.gap: Regular Riesz-calibrated transport theory assumes enough overlap for a square-integrable representer, whereas irregular inverse-weight theory does not compute the sharp two-sample Hölder boundary frontier or its critical logarithm.
project_justification.niche: Polynomial trial depletion with a positive target boundary density creates an estimable causal mean whose information geometry changes exactly at \(a=1\); the target sample also imposes a separate parametric floor.
project_justification.fill: Under the separate primitive requirements \(t>1/2\) for density-ratio sieve calibration and \(s/(2s+1)+t/(2t+1)>1/2\) for the nuisance-product remainder, the project derives the matching modulus, derives optimizer stability for an executable calibrated-transport plus local-polynomial estimator, and provides fixed-class honest intervals with a fold-centered joint calibration--boundary multiplier envelope and an explicit covariance-complete standard error while making the self-similarity requirement for adaptation explicit.

related_work: Burman et al. (2026) are the optimization and application anchor, not a nested estimand comparator. Their target unit contains an observed outcome. Proposition 2.1 on page 6 identifies \(\tau_Q=\mathbb E_Q[Y^Q]-\mathbb E_Q[\mu_0(X^Q)]\), while Theorem 3.1 on pages 6--7 gives its efficient influence function; this core instead observes only target covariates and targets \(\mathbb E_{P_T}[\mu_1(X)-\mu_0(X)]\). Their Assumption 1(iv) on page 7 imposes bounded target-to-trial density ratio, Theorem 4.5 on pages 13--14 proves calibrated-weight consistency, Theorem 5.2 on page 16 gives efficient inference for their estimand, and Section 8 on pages 23--24 studies 30-month mortality in transthyretin amyloid cardiomyopathy. Section S4.3 is the source locator for the standard one-dimensional density-ratio calibration-sieve threshold \(t>1/2\). That threshold is separate from \(s/(2s+1)+t/(2t+1)>1/2\), which controls the distinct nuisance-product remainder. The present transport program is informed by their semi-unbalanced entropic geometry without claiming that its \(a=0\) case reproduces their theorem.
